newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index stages late rally, SBI up 6.20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index stages late rally, SBI up 6.20 pct.

text.p: A late rally inspired by hectic local bidding in shares of State Bank of India (SBI) helped Bombay stocks on Tuesday resume their ascent after a lacklustre early session, dealers said.
"The market showed a kind of weakness early on..but spurted in the latter half of trading..," said dealer Vetri Subramaniam at institutional brokerage SSKI Securities.
Subramaniam said the buying appeared to be traders short-covering.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top index surged 41.49 points, or over one percent to end at a provisional 3,604.23.
SBI shot up 18.25 rupees, or 6.20 percent, to finish at 312.75 in hectic volumes of 1.04 billion shares, thus making it one of the best performing bellwether stocks on Tuesday.
Market talk of a relaxation in the 20 percent foreign buying limit in SBI spurred the price rise, dealers said.

"This will help a great deal to stoke up buying appetite of foreign institutional investors," said senior trader Ramnik Parekh. He said continued speculative buying ahead of government announcements was likely to sustain the market's upward trend.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Monday said new economic policy measures would be announced in the next few days.
Deve Gowda said the government would announce the policy measures this week before he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram leave to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos on January 31.
"Some decisions will be coming in the next two to three days," the prime minister told a business gathering in Bombay.
Tuesday's BSE index rise came on the back of nearly a four percent surge on Monday.
Dealers said hesitation by operators to take delivery of stocks on the last day of settlement at the National Stock Exchange helped pviotals end lower than BSE rates.
TISCO rose 3.0 rupees to 211.0 and Reliance 8.0 to 280.50.
